name: Alain Guillotin
desc: The founder of the Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering, with his most notable contribution to Fontaine being his research in Pneuma-Ousia, which led to the invention of the Arkhe system and the creation of Clockwork Meka.

desc.text:
...
The assigned assistant doesn't seem very reliable.
At the moment, it doesn't look like the power sources of those war machines can be used. Their cores are far too dangerous.
I'll get them to seek out other such mysterious machines.
...
No progress worth reporting today.
Went out with Ann under the watchful eyes of my adoptive father to look for inspiration at sites where battles took place. Ran into Rene and Jakob.
...
The assistant doesn't seem reliable. Caused some accidents. Just another obstacle to overcome.
This kind of machine with the seemingly arbitrary external form is quite interesting. Research will focus on their power source.
...
Researched primenergy machines.
Assistant took the day off.
Asked Ann for help.
Recommended Rene and Jakob to the director of the Institute.
...
Researched primenergy machines.
Assistant took the day off.
Asked Ann for help. Suggested she join the Institute, but she wasn't interested.
...
Researched primenergy machines.
My assistant still isn't back. I'll go to pay a visit.
Found Rene and Jakob's adoptive father with my own adoptive father's help.
...
The supplementary primenergy machines have arrived. Should be able to make progress now.
Assistant seems to be in good spirits. Probably just a minor illness.
...
Researched primenergy machines.
Rene and Jakob joined the Institute. They've been assigned to my project.
...
Field research today.
Interesting machine statue.
...
Researched primenergy machines.
...
Researched primenergy machines.
My adoptive father visited, but I was too busy to host him. Ann scolded me. I'll remember to apologize next time I see him.
...
Researched primenergy machines.
Assistant took the day off.
...
On the threshold of a major breakthrough.
Assistant took the day off. I was too busy to visit. Ann scolded me. I'll go tomorrow.
...
On the threshold of a major breakthrough.
Forgot about the visit, am sorry. Will invite everyone to go with me.
...
Took the day off.
Assistant took the day off. Went to visit.
An idea: a virtual neural network based on a vast quantity of thinking units instead of logic trees.
A Kamera?
...
Researched primenergy machines.
Assistant took the day off.
...
Researched primenergy machines.
Assistant took the day off.
...
Researched primenergy machines.
Rene and Jakob went to begin conducting their own research today.
Assistant took the day off.
...
A breakthrough.
Patent application process is too annoying. Forget it.
Assistant's condition seems okay. Still a little worried.
Considering the gap in medical technology, advised assistant to go to Sumeru.
...
Took the day off.
Researching machine kinematics next.
Must make a materials list.
...
Visit.
...
Visit.
...
Visit.
They said a bigger lab has been prepared for the kinematic experiments.
But I've decided not to move for now.
...
Visit.
...
Visit.
...
Visit.
Been urged to move the lab several times.
But if the lab is moved, my assistant might not be able to find it. A pain.
...
Visit.
...
Visit.
...
Visit.
Moved my lab.

...
...I was assigned to the same lab. I was nervous at first, since everyone said that he was a child prodigy. Since the disaster, such people are even more precious.
I thought that since he's a star of the Institute and was recommended by higher-ups, he'd be full of himself, but he's much better than I expected. He's just not especially nice or anything...
No obvious symptoms.
...
...I made a huge mistake, and knocked over an ancient geometry machine that took a lot of effort to bring back from the desert ruins. But then the machine came to life, and messed everything up...
...Though he's a lot younger than me, he's really smart. I can't believe that's how he managed to tame the machine. Maybe taming isn't the right word? Maybe the other engineers will look down on me for using it. But it really did feel like taming... I know the current clockwork machines pretty well, so I can tell the huge technological gulf between the two. Ignoring structure, if we can't solve the power source problems, then it'll be difficult to make any meaningful progress...
...But I still have to be careful. I've never seen Alain angry, and I don't want to find out what he looks like when he gets angry.
A few minor symptoms have appeared.
...
Took the day off.
...
I can hardly believe it! Alain came to visit me, and even brought his sister! She's cute and not afraid of strangers. I'm so happy...
...We discussed the idea of a thinking machine based on gems and tape circuits. I used the word "discussed," but actually I just said things like "Oh!" or "That's really amazing" or "How will you do that?" whenever he paused, and didn't make any real contributions. He was really into it, though, and he behaved very differently than he usually does in the lab. His little sister is probably way smarter than me, a research assistant!
...I guess it isn't that boring when it flares up, but I want to return to the Institute to help as soon as I can...
...
...The additional machines got here. The previous ones are no longer usable since they were completely dismantled... But it did clear up a lot of things, at least according to him. Something about it being driven by the elements in the ley lines, but we can't recreate it with our current level of industrial precision and material science. I helped with compiling the report, but there's so much I couldn't understand!
...Apparently, lots of people are secretly unhappy that Alain has more research resources than them... But if you ask me, everyone's smarter than me, and they should all get along, that way we can make the world a better place.
...His sister said that some of their friends are joining the Institute. I'm looking forward to meeting them...
No obvious symptoms.
...
...joined the lab as new partners! But now I'm even more confused by their conversations! Why is it I can understand every word on its own, but once they string them all together, I can't make heads or tails of it? Jakob is really the only one even close to being on the same level as me... I feel ashamed just writing that, as an adult looking for reassurance from a child as young as Jakob, I feel like I've lost all the self-respect an adult should have...
...Based on their research on Primenergy Machinery (seems like they decided to adopt this name), Alain and Rene are thinking about trying to use the characteristics of ousia and pneuma to construct a new kinetic core...
A few minor symptoms.
...
...I may have made a contribution! Well, maybe? I went on a picnic with Alain, his sister, Rene, and Jakob. It was technically supposed to be field research, but the idea came from Alain's sister and me. We thought they didn't have any life at all outside of their research, so we asked the Institute's director to arrange something...
...Petrichor's quite boring, but the scenery is quite nice, since you can see the great waterfall. I brought a Kamera from the Institute to take photos for them. I hope there are more outings like this one in the future so I can take more photos of his sister especially. After all, Alain is always working and can't be with his sister as she grows up, so these photos will come in handy later when he regrets not spending much time with her. Then he'll be able to see how she was at different times, and it won't sting so much! If only my family had enough money for a Kamera and things didn't go wrong, I'm sure my mom would have taken lots of photos of me... Rene and Jakob like Alain's sister a lot, too. When the four of them hang out, she sometimes acts like an older sister to them, despite being the youngest, it's a really interesting dynamic...
...Seem to be interested in the ruins and the stone statues here. Rene also mentioned something about a troupe and seals... Even though we went out there to have a bit of fun for once, they were still thinking about research...
No obvious symptoms.
...
Took the day off.
...
...Alain's sister came to see me with Jakob. Alain and Rene couldn't make it, because their experiment is at a critical stage. They didn't have to tell me any of that though, after all, with my limited abilities, that I was able to help at all is already fulfilling!
...
I heard that Alain and the Institute's director came to see me (separately)! while I was unconscious. I feel bad that they came all this way for nothing, I wasn't even awake...
Still taking time off, but I hope to go back and help them again soon.
...
...I found out that they were graduates from the Narzissenkreuz Institute, and that made me really happy. They talked about the director and the vice director, as well as their adventures, and it made me feel like a kid again. The only detail that didn't make sense was the cake the vice director made, because it felt like punishment when we had it...
...After the disaster, I lost contact with pretty much all my friends. I'm so happy that they were able to find each other again. I wonder how my friends are doing. They're probably trying to rebuild the Narzissenkreuz Institute! Next time I'll go check it out...
...Talked about the thinking machine again. I had an idea about making a thinking Kamera, so that it would take photos of those precious to him while he's busy. He thought it was kind of pointless, but that it had security and surveillance applications...
...
...They did it! The light bulb came on! I was lucky to have recovered in time to witness this historical moment... It's quite a pity, but I hope Rene and Jakob will make the breakthroughs of their own in their own research topics! Ah, I also hope they get better assistants than me!
No clear symptoms.
...
Took the day off.
...
There were several visits while I was unconscious. It's a shame, all I could do is read the letters they left behind.
Jakob left me a note, inviting me to his and Rene's lab. There's something they want to talk to me about.
I hope I can get out of bed soon.
...
Ann brought flowers for me, but they had already wilted by the time I woke up.
Took the day off.
...
I was able to get out of bed today.
This is where I first met Alain. For a time afterwards, my first time standing here I documented the experimental procedures and phenomena based on his oral descriptions. He was trying to start up the machinery below in an ill-fitting lab coat. Rene and Jakob later entered through that door, and Alain would temporarily forget to act the young genius, and rush towards them like an energetic kid.
I found myself witness to the first successful controlled annihilation reaction. The brilliant light cast a deep, dark shadow and I believe history was made in that moment. Can someone like me, so excited I knocked over the ink bottle, play a role in such a historical event?
Behind the locked door on the other side is Rene and Jakob's lab. It seems access was limited due to the dangerous nature of their research. They are destined to become towering figures in history.
I guess Alain moved to another lab. Based on his plan, once the energy problem was solved, he would study kinematics. I'll go greet him later. I wonder how Ann is doing now? I wonder what kind of beautiful woman she will grow up to be?
I'll stop writing here. I don't have much time left.
I hope everything goes well.

...
...Following Guillotin's instructions, the research went well... We've created a clockwork meka that can release energy. To be honest, we no longer need to call it a clockwork machine as it doesn't rely on elastic potential... It'll be compelling to see what results he achieves next in kinematics. There's no way old-fashioned clockwork meka can withstand such power output. Even young geniuses must stumble now and then...
...
...The thought of using this sort of unstable energy source is impressive. Though we have long observed these unique energies in Fontaine's atmosphere, water, and organisms, it has always been regarded as a latent threat, rather than a potential resource...
...
...Aren't there a few young geniuses too many nowadays? The director is pleased, sure, but won't someone spare a thought for us ordinary people? I mean, not all of us are as simpleminded as Scherbius...
...
...It received a very high rating. If the patent were to be granted, the potential financial gain would be considerable. However, I decided to decline the opportunity, because the machine was practically all Guillotin's work, and I can take no credit there. My family was quite angry about it, but as an engineer, one must have at least a little dignity and self-awareness...
...Still making improvements, and output efficiency has increased...
...
...Seems to have been specially recruited. That's good. Had he continued that line of research, who knows what horrors he might have unleashed...
...
...At this stage, we have to pull out. The director says everyone will be given a position and research resources after reconstruction, but I'm afraid if it were me, I would use this as an excuse for a major shake-up. People like me won't get recalled anyway. Never mind. I've been pretty happy these past few days, I guess I'll consider it my retirement. I'll go to the city and open a small workshop, repairing watches for folks, Kameras too. Right, I'll see if I can make a waterproof clock. With the way things are going, I might make a killing in the future.

...
...It seems the ordinary Dahri machines can no longer satisfy him. As a result, the director used national resources to obtain something truly horrifying. Rumor has it that someone was nearly killed! I hope this will help him achieve his research objectives... They even got him some rare Dahri mechanical parts being studied by Sumeru researchers as part of the package...
...
...Things went out of control for a third time! Guillotin may be willing to risk his own life, but that doesn't mean the rest of us feel the same... I came up with an emergency damage control strategy, and I hope we won't need to use it before he finishes his kinematics research. However, given his personality, it seems unlikely that he'll ever truly complete that research...
...
...It seems that his experiments into machines were intended to create a mechanical dog as proof of his accomplishments in kinematics and material science. It's actually a good idea and could be showcased in the city, and the creature is much more personable and likable compared to the automated turret next door...
...
...At least he lived long enough to be poached by the Marechaussee Hunters. It wasn't easy for us to survive this long, either. But what will we do with this blasted crazy killing machine that can repair itself!? Whatever... That's a problem for future generations...

...
...Anyway, when it comes down to it, our research directions are different, so I applied for a new research lab with the director. But there's nothing for it anyway. Alain is incredibly intelligent, but he only trusts himself, and doesn't trust our observations or accomplishments unless he reaches the same conclusions through his own calculations. Well, it's okay, since Alain is making the world a better place in his own way. I trust him, because this is the world that Ann lives in...
...Even though the Institute is full of people, I don't have many friends besides Carter. It feels like everyone kinda dislikes us...
...Rene managed to acquire something powerful to research. Apparently these appeared after the disaster, and are very dangerous for most people. But I feel okay, maybe my constitution really has gotten a lot better...
...I helped Rene out!
...When I visited him, I found out that he also attended Narzissenkreuz Institute. We didn't tell him about the Vice Director abandoning us, or it would have made him sad... If only we could have helped him just like I was helped...
...
...After discussing it with Rene, he finally agreed to give it a try. He said since it's dangerous everything needs to be made clear to Carter and he must make the judgment himself as it concerns his own life. But, if it's successful, then he'll survive just like I did...

"Destroying this █████ board will be seen as a challenge to national authority, and violators will be publicly sentenced on charges of ███████."

(...The reverse side has the seal of the courts and the signatures of Alain Guillotin and Neuvillette.)

textualResearch.title: (This is a strange fairy tale with some comments written in purple ink.)

desc.text:
The rabbit's pocket watch is, in truth, the beginning of the dream. The watch is a precise timekeeper, but the flow of time in dreamland is madness. When the clock chimes, all shall end.
Mary-Ann, whom people often mistake Liddell for... But could it not be that they were, at first, one and the same?
The caterpillar has all the hallmarks of maturity. The pipe, the reading glasses, the knowledge. Yet a larva he remains, not yet a butterfly. One who lacks the confidence to break through a cocoon shall die before ever becoming so. But moths have no mouthparts, and thus they can only leap into the flames.
The Queen of Hearts, the one who loved to take heads.
The White Knight, who mumbled about his little inventions.
The Red Queen... In the end, it was all her dream, and she was a little mother cat.

"To my little Clockwork Princess..."
"If you're reading this..."
"You've most likely received the 'gift' I left for you. I just hope you didn't stumble across all this while cleaning out my effects, or something trivial like that."
"I once asked if there was something you wished for. Do you remember that? I wonder if time has changed your answer..."
"Regardless, I have another gift — a formula that will allow you to come face to face with the 'anomaly' inside of you. Haha... if you even still call her that."
"Why this gift? To understand that, allow me to wax poetic on the soul once again. I would ask you to stick with me until the end, but I know you will. You always have."
"I believe a person should be born twice over in their lifetime. First, there's the birth that grants us life, then the birth of the soul."
"It's a matter of transforming the life bestowed upon us into the life we choose for ourselves. And to do that, we must look inward.
"We must make a conscious choice to define the meaning of our life, instead of allowing the happenstance of our existence to pass us by..."
"This is the process of recognizing the 'soul' that lives within us."
"You are my proudest masterpiece. I told you that long ago. But to me, you have never been a creation or a machine."
"To me, you're just like the rest of us. You have a heart."
"In fact, some theories think of the human brain as nothing more than a machine, and thought the product of its computations."
"So, you see? Perhaps we're not so different, after all. Your inner machinery is just far more advanced than most."
"No matter how one looks at it, the heart is a complex thing... a place where logic and reason collide with our emotions.
"Your computational capacity allowed you to become sentient and develop logical reasoning. But it also granted you something that, on the surface, might seem contradictory — emotion."
"Emotions and logic often clash with each other, and those instances of discord can accumulate over time. That is the source of what you refer to as the 'anomalies' within you."
"As you told me once, you've always known what you don't want. Yet, you've never wished for anything in particular."
"Similar to how a blind person can feel when a part of their
is in pain, without being able to fully visualize its form. Such is your relationship with your soul."
"So, what I leave you now is this... a formula that will allow you to see the shape of your soul. For if you want to protect your 'heart,' you must first be able to recognize it within yourself."
"Of course, whether you use it is entirely up to you. You are, and always have been, free to do as you wish."
"Regardless, whether by my formula or some other means, I trust you will know your heart one day. You always were a fast learner... and the smartest person I've ever known."

customize.name: Recon Log Mek
customize.desc:
One of the earliest new-type clockwork meka to be made.

It is said that during his time at the Institute of Natural Philosophy, the Lord-Artificer Guillotin created machines that could simulate genuine intelligence.

Though he never openly admitted it, this rumor nonetheless spurred on subsequent generations of ambitious engineers. Decades ago, one of them announced that they had created a machine that not only possessed basic thinking abilities but could also read human emotions, but in the end the results went unacknowledged.

customize.name: Arithmetic Enhancer Mek
customize.desc:
A clockwork meka designed to transmit and enhance signals.

The power that drives this clockwork meka is generated from a controlled annihilation reaction between ousia and pneuma in the kinetic core. As a result, overloading it with excessive energy will cause its original equilibrium to be disrupted.

customize.name: Underwater Survey Mek
customize.desc:
A clockwork meka designed for underwater surveying.

In the absence of significant breakthroughs in dynamics research, kinematics research has had the most significant impact on clockwork meka design. For machines designed to perform specific tasks, biomimesis has sometimes provided the most convenient solutions.

customize.name: Geological Survey Mek
customize.desc:
A clockwork meka designed for surveying underground resources and certain minerals.

Due to the fact that the desired metal type can be set, this device has proven very popular among Treasure Hoarders and Adventurers alike.

customize.name: Underwater Patrol Mek
customize.desc:
This type of clockwork meka was designed to search out, repel, and if need be exterminate aquatic life forms that pose a threat to underwater equipment.

Ever since the first diluvian period, the Fontaine Research Institute has been preoccupied with the thought that there might be a second one. Some had the idea of taking back the ruins lost to the waves and building an underwater city, whereas others looked up to the untouchable sky islands overhead with the intention of building a metropolis in the clouds.

Underwater Patrol Meks were conceived by the former, but judging from the results, it is the latter that have gained the upper hand in recent years.

customize.name: Nimble Harvester Mek
customize.desc:
A clockwork meka designed to dig up and transport soil.

Due to the inherent ability of the local water and soil to store and transmit ousia and pneuma, clockwork meka powered by the annihilation of these energies are highly favored in Fontaine. This also explains why adventurers may come across Ousia and Pneuma Blocks from time to time.

customize.name: Area Alert Mek
customize.desc:
A mechanism that is able to fire out the energy produced by an annihilation reaction. Strictly speaking, it was originally a test device that emerged from research undertaken by the Institute of Natural Philosophy before the Fontaine Research Institute had been established.

As such, despite its considerable commercial success as a sentinel and defensive device, most engineers do not consider it to be a true clockwork meka.

customize.name: Assault Specialist Mek
customize.desc:
Alongside the Recon Log Mek, this was one of the first new-type clockwork meka to be made (though of course, after hundreds of years, no one refers to them as "new-type" anymore – this was simply to differentiate them from traditional clockwork mechanisms that were powered by potential energy.)

It was named to commemorate a friend of its inventor, and was originally designed to help people. However, its ability to attack people – thereby avoiding the need to put friendly personnel at risk – subsequently came to be seen as its real strength.

customize.name: Suppression Specialist Mek
customize.desc:
A clockwork meka adapted from the Cal. Scherbius type. Unfortunately, aside from its ability to attack, it has no other capabilities.

Clockwork meka based on annihilation energy normally produce their energy by utilizing Repeaters composed of special crystals to refine ousia and pneuma from Fontaine's environment. But outside of Fontaine, they can use pre-prepared Energy Blocks to move over short distances for short periods of time. The difference can be observed from the shape of the crystal components on the meka.

customize.name: Annihilation Specialist Mek
customize.desc:
Although the Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering is the main organization involved in clockwork meka research and design, there are also many independent engineers and workshops that are not affiliated with the Research Institute.

The first ever machine of this type was designed by an independent engineer to commemorate their lover and sponsor. In the end, it was acquired by the Maison Gardiennage as a tool to uphold municipal security — or, as some would have it, state apparatus enforcing the monopoly on violence.

customize.name: Construction Specialist Mek
customize.desc:
A type of large clockwork meka which also has immeasurable value when utilized in building construction and archeological excavation. Its name comes from an engineer employed by Callas during the construction of the Clementine Line.

With Callas' financial backing, this engineer built the legendary "Golden Vessel" — a gigantic piece of construction machinery which was used to dig the Poisson Tunnel. Once the job was complete, this type of clockwork meka was designed with a similar structure but reduced to a smaller scale.

customize.text: Character Story

<color=#ffd680>Character Details</color>
Alain Guillotin would call her Marionette. Behind this name was the story of a loved one he could not forget and whose memories he had naively tried to revive by creating her. But the moment she opened her eyes and tentatively spoke his name, he resolved never to call her that again. It was wrong, he realized, to make this exquisite little creation bear the weight of his sister's life, and of his own mistake. This little creation deserved a life of her very own, just like anyone else born into this world.
But from time to time, he still addressed her by that name, if only in his thoughts. He did so because, just as the name "Marionette" suggested, she was pure of heart, kind, and always full of joy.
The people of Snezhnaya knew her as "the Lady" or "Lady Marionette." While most spoke of her with the fear that a Harbinger typically inspires, there was also often a distinct note of respect in their voices, a sentiment made clear by descriptions such as "the decisive Lady Marionette" and "the ever-reliable Lady Marionette."
But to her friends and colleagues, she was known as Sandrone. While it was originally just a code name, over time the name became a cheerful way for her closest and dearest to address her. They began to associate it with the scents of desserts and afternoon tea, with the elegant turning of book pages and the steady ticking of a mainspring.... And of course, at times, it also evoked the grumbles and even furious outbursts of a lady who had lost all patience, proper etiquette be damned.
Once, a friend put this question to her: "What do you want us to call you?"
"It doesn't matter, and I don't really care," she replied nonchalantly. "I've always thought names to be something that existed mainly for the convenience of others. What other people choose to call me is, to a very large extent, determined by which part of me they choose to accept."
The expression on her friend's face was one that clearly suggested that they were woefully unprepared for her answer.
"Anyhow, what I mean to say is: No matter what people choose to call me, I am still myself. I will not change because they have chosen to call me by a different name, and since I do not care for what people call me, why not just let them use the name they're most comfortable with? But as to whether I would respond to the name in question, that is another matter altogether, heh."
<color=#ffd680>Character Story 1</color>
She remembers very clearly the day she was born.
First, it was dark. She opened her eyes, and began to scan everything around her. She realized that she was sitting on a chair, and that right before her was a man who looked rather old. He told her his name was Alain Guillotin.
She repeated the name, then asked what her name was. The old man did not reply for a while, as if he had just been confronted with something he had never considered before. But in the end, he spoke with some hesitation, a look she had yet to understand crossing his face. "Marionette..."
"Marionette." She repeated the name.
The old man's face became even more contorted by some kind of emotion. That is strange, she thought. Why is it that I can identify just about everything I see in my field of vision, but can't quite name what he is feeling? I should put this in my list of questions to be answered.
And that list was a rather long one. For example, why was she here? How did she come to be, and what is the purpose of it? How do you dice a potato so that the pieces are perfectly uniform and so presentable enough for dinner? And what do you have to do so that the plant on the windowsill would yield the most gorgeous blooms...?
The answers to certain things, she learned, were easily found. In most cases, these simply required her to invest some time and engage in some straightforward learning. But other questions were far more profound, so profound that even the old man who made her were unable to answer.
She spent most of her time with the old man, Alain Guillotin. At some point, she discovered that she did not like him very much at all. He moved too slowly, and was thoroughly disorganized. He would often misplace his papers and tools, and from time to time, he would even hand her a notebook that served no practical purpose.
"Your life is a total mess," she said to him point-blank. "Your things are never where they belong, and your papers are scattered everywhere. You write a single equation across two sheets, only for them to somehow end up at opposite ends of the room."
In the face of her unfiltered complaints, an odd smile appeared on the old man's face, as if he had just been praised for something. "Haha... That was exactly what Mary-Ann used to say about me, too."
That man was simply impossible to understand.
But over time, she also came to discover the parts of the old man she liked better.
She grew fond of the way he was so utterly focused while deep in his work, and the sound of his pen against paper. She cherished the way he would explain various principles of engineering to her, and the way he discussed complex math problems with her at the workbench. She found comfort in the stories he would tell her about the past while sitting by the fire, about the Fontaine of old, about Nymph's Croix... And she held a quiet appreciation for the gentle smile on his face in those moments.
She discovered that although this old man was rather careless and disorganized, he was also kind, righteous, and full of wisdom.
As time passed, the parts she liked about the old man came to vastly outnumber the parts she did not. This led her to embark on a review of her previous actions.
Alain was stunned when he found her writing in her notebook.
She could tell that he really, really wanted to ask her what she was doing, but for fear of making her change her mind, he forced himself to swallow his curiosity.
She decided to take the initiative. "I think I dislike you," she said.
She could tell that he was rather hurt by that opener.
"But I also discovered that I was wrong. That was a judgment made at a time when my base emotional logic and objectivity were not yet fully in place." She continued: "But now, I feel that you are a very good 'father.'"
Alain was astonished for a moment. Then, a smile appeared on his face. It was a smile of genuine happiness mixed with some other emotion.
Is he... going to cry? She was still slowly learning to read human emotions, though she still couldn't understand the reason behind them.
But that question could wait. She picked up her notebook and started writing again.
<color=#ffd680>Character Story 2</color>
She remembers Alain's passing very, very clearly.
Alain was bedbound for some time before his death, and during this time, he relied entirely on her to care for his day-to-day needs. In the beginning, he was still able to respond to her and to converse with her, listening as she recounted the fresh news and gossip she had gathered while out on her errands. But as time wore on, all he wanted to do was to lie quietly in his bed.
As she sat by his bedside and read to him, she would hear a long, labored rasp from his throat from time to time. It sounded as though Alain were being suffocated by his own breath, or as if he were being held by the throat by the air itself.
When Alain created her, he had given her the sense of touch, the sense of taste, and even breath, which served as a cooling system to regulate her body temperature. But now, in the final chapter of his life, all these things were being taken from Alain one by one. First went his sense of taste, then his sense of touch, and finally, his breath.
There were several moments where she thought he would simply falter and fade. This is his final breath, she would think to herself. But he would pull through, again and again, every single time.
One of these times, when she glanced over at the bed, she noticed that Alain had opened his eyes and was looking at her.
"I thought I was done this time," he said.
"Done? Done what?"
"I thought I'd finally gone to another place," he chuckled. "I've been practicing how to die."
He wished to pass on in his sleep, he explained. Better yet, he wished to pass on in the middle of a beautiful dream, a dream where he would be lying on a grassy lawn looking up at the blue, blue skies of Fontaine, together with his friends and his sister.
"Am I in that dream too?" she asked.
"Oh, no, no," he replied. "You do not belong to the world I am heading to, my child. You have a very long road ahead of you here on this side."
"Do you wish to go to that world?"
Alain let out a long sigh.
"It's no longer a matter of whether I wish to at this point." He turned his head to look at the ceiling, as if he could look through it to another world beyond. "No one truly knows the taste of death, for it is a fruit that one can only savor once in a lifetime."
"It sounds to me like it tastes pretty awful."
"Haha... Maybe." Alain chuckled again, though she did not know what was funny about her words.
"But it is rarely the dead who suffer," He went on. "The true pain is borne by the ones left behind."
This seemed to be some sort of prediction as well as personal reflection on Alain's part. And whatever this was, he was right.
She continued to go out to the shops after Alain's death, even though there was no one home to use whatever she bought any more. She still tended to the garden and maintained Pulonia, although she had no idea why she did so.
Maybe she hadn't had enough time to accept the truth. Or maybe, she simply did not know what else she could do. She pondered this, and the thought left her deeply unsettled.
"Go. Do what you want to do, and seek out your own desires, my child."
For some unknown reason, she had started thinking about Alain's final words to her.
But there's nothing I want to do, and I desire nothing, she told herself.
But I should go look for it, she thought.
"Alright, Alain," she spoke to the vacancy of the empty bed. "Looks like it's my turn now."
"It's my turn to practice living."
<color=#ffd680>Character Story 5</color>
With the "inheritance" she received from Alain, Sandrone was able to welcome her second birth.
She had always believed she was smart, or at least smarter than most. It was only at this juncture that she realized she was actually far more foolish than she had thought.
She told herself she should have gotten there a long time ago. She should have listened to her heart to understand what words like "loss" and "to endure" really meant. She should have expressed her gratitude to her friends more and made more friends. She should have returned to Fontaine long ago, to Alain's graveside... where she would tell him all about what's happened to her since she left while tidying up his grave.
But it was never too late to start, Columbina told her. Columbina herself had learned this from someone else.
She let out a little snort. Never did she imagine that she would be receiving life lessons from Columbina one day. But she accepted it anyway. There was no denying it: Columbina was right.
When news of Sandrone's resurrection reached Snezhnograd, words of sympathy and concern quickly followed, alongside a generous offer of "post-mortem leave" from her position. However, when Sandrone expressed her desire to remain with the Fatui instead, the Tsaritsa naturally agreed without further comment.
She knew this news would cause unhappiness in certain quarters, for it meant the power and interests carved up upon her death had suddenly vanished from their grasp.
But she did not care what the others would think. She had just been given a second life, and she was going to live it exactly the way she liked. She was going to live entirely on her own terms now, and she certainly wasn't going to hold her tongue when she got mad! Ha! Did that certain someone really think he was going to take control of the Adventurers' Guild, of Katheryne and the rest of them, from now on? Fat chance!
But of course, that did not mean she was entirely free from the shackles of life. Every time she received word of yet another Fatui meeting, she would roll her eyes and grumble as always.
"Pfft. Meetings, and more meetings! All day, every day! Annoying!"
<color=#ffd680>Pulonia</color>
The first time Sandrone met the behemoth, it immediately extended its hand to her.
That's just his humanoid programming, Alain told her. Pulonia, short for the "Prospective Undulation Localized Observing and Investigating Automaton," was built for measurements and calculations. Nevertheless, he hoped these human-like additions would allow the world to see Pulonia as more than just a machine, because just like her, Pulonia was also one of a kind.
She was delighted by the new family member in her life. She took Pulonia on walks, where she would teach it to identify the various flowers and birds they came across. But Pulonia was a slow learner, far slower than she was. According to Alain, this was because Pulonia's core processing power was dedicated to predicting the future via simulation.
But why do that, she asked.
Alain then said something she would understand only much later. At the time, she only thought Pulonia was impressive, and she even envied Pulonia a little. Why couldn't she do something so amazing herself?
But like Alain, this amazing giant needed looking after, too. He would frequently get stuck halfway through their walks, or somehow get wet from the water meant for the flowers. She had no choice but to learn the ins and outs of Pulonia's workings to tune him when needed, as if she was looking after her baby brother. And this continued even after Alain passed away.
The day Sandrone returned from Alain's funeral service, she was like a wind-up toy with a jammed spring. All she could do was stand silently in her room with her raincoat on, unable to even move or even close the main door.
Then, she noticed Pulonia lumbering towards her, and like the very first time they met, he extended his huge hand to her.
She stared at that hand. It was so massive, capable of holding up the future of the entire world — and from this day forward, it would also have to anchor her past. This was a loss utterly unbearable for her, the void it left behind nearly enough to crush her. Every bit of that burden now fell upon Pulonia, and he would bear the weight without a single whisper of complaint.
Although Pulonia did, eventually, hold up the future of the entire world... He could no longer support his own weight.
Sandrone has not given up on fixing Pulonia ever since. But she knows that with her current knowledge and skillset, she is far from able to fully restore Pulonia's core. More importantly, she refuses to settle for a compromised restoration, bringing back a "Pulonia" that would no longer recognize her, for that would be a complete insult to the great Pulonia, and to the family he was to her.
And so, she arranged for Pulonia to be returned to a secret location, that home they used to share, and she would visit Pulonia every now and then.
One day, she hopes, her devotion will reward her with the familiar, clattering sound of Pulonia starting up anew, as he extends that giant hand to her just like he used to.
<color=#ffd680>Stellar Linchpin</color>
Sandrone has not relied very much on the Stellar Linchpin ever since it came into her possession. Certainly, she is aware that it was this little rock that activated her "inheritance" from Alain and gave her the second life, a fact for which she is grateful. But she remains troubled by a simple problem: She can't quite see how this little thing is supposed to be of any real help in her daily life.
Is it supposed to help her with her research? But that's what her brains are for... It's not like the Stellar Linchpin can solve equations for her.
Or is it meant to help her channel elemental energy? But even before she ever had it, she rarely relied on elemental energy to fight.
Or maybe, it provides some kind of energy support? But no matter how she looks at it, it does not appear to be compatible with her body structure. After all, thanks to the great Alain Guillotin, Lord-Artificer, she already runs on a core power supply system that is pretty much perfect...
Eventually, she settles on using the Cryo in the Stellar Linchpin as a cooling well for herself and Fagio during heavy-duty computing tasks. Additionally, to ensure combat and energy efficiency, she has also temporarily adapted Fagio's attack logic to work with the Stellar Linchpin.
And if anyone asked Sandrone what her wish was, she would only say that the word "wish" is both too hazy and too complicated. All she wants is to deconstruct the universal principles of all things and continuously lay the bedrock of knowledge — but does that count as a wish? Certainly. But is that all she wishes for? Of course not.
Right now, she is doing what she wants to do, and what she thinks is right. This alone makes her happy, and perhaps that is more than enough. Who is to say that the call of a wish such as this just isn't compelling enough? And who is to say that choosing to lead the life one wants isn't right? One wish shouldn't be considered nobler than another. To her mind, everyone has their own life to live, and if anyone has a problem with that, they had better be prepared for a verbal shelling from Sandrone. And if they still have a problem after that, she'd probably just scoff and point a cheeky finger up at the sky...
Saying, "Well, then you'd better take it up with the one who came up with this!"
Voice-Over

<color=#ffd680>About Sandrone: Name</color>
What's wrong with calling me Sandrone? Huh...? My original name? Hah... So, you really want to know? Alright, alright... I can still remember when I first opened my eyes. Alain had just finished creating me. He called me "Marionette." I tried to repeat it, to say it out loud myself, but I noticed something... complicated in his expression. Only later did I come to understand what it was — a mixture of regret and guilt. He never called me that again. Anyway, after telling me the story of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo and his sister, Alain concluded by insisting that I was free to choose my own path in life. An important part of that, he said, was deciding on my own name. For my part, I told him I was perfectly fine with the one he'd given me. "Marionette Guillotin"... Pretty unique as names go, wouldn't you say? And yet, no doubt for different reasons, the Tsaritsa ended up making "Marionette" my title as a Harbinger. Heh... Perhaps that was simply another so-called "act of fate."
<color=#ffd680>Something to Share</color>
With Pulonia gone, life suddenly felt a lot more difficult to navigate. That's why I created Fagio — my "Facilitatrice Automatisee Generaliste Interactive et Omnitache." She can deal with a lot of trivial tasks that I'd rather not waste my time with — and she can fight. Huh? You think her full name's too long and... hard to understand? Is that not how all working machines get their names? Alain came up with Pulonia, which stands for "Prospective Undulation Localized Observing and Investigating Automaton." I thought everyone named things that way. So, you think it's hereditary...?
<color=#ffd680>Interesting Things</color>
Outside of my research, I sometimes like to ponder metaphysical questions. Just as people from every nation have their own beliefs about death. I often hear people talking about the "afterlife," "where souls go to rest," things like that... But from the time my core was damaged fighting Il Dottore, to the time the "Stellar Linchpin" activated Alain's legacy and reactivated me, my memory is blank — completely empty. Where do mechanical constructs, "puppets," go when they die? How are our "souls" defined? Do we even have souls? There are no answers, so I always turn back to my research. But knowledge is the cornerstone of the world. I believe that as these stones continue to stack, one day their height alone will allow me to reach the answers to my doubts.
<color=#ffd680>About Alain Guillotin</color>
After Alain died, I put up a tombstone for him. When he was alive, he said he wanted me to write his epitaph. So I did. It wasn't difficult — list out his deeds, then pick a quote that captures the way he thought. I went with, "Regrettably, there's nothing more to say." It was something he often said. You think it sounds fatalistic? Hah, maybe to those who didn't know him. But he always said it with a smile. It wasn't resignation — he wasn't giving up. Ironically, it was almost like an expression of contentment. Like solving a mathematical problem. Death is just a silent equals sign, and he's moved to the other side of the equation.
<color=#ffd680>More About Sandrone: III</color>
It never bothered me that Alain created me to look like his sister Mary-Ann — or that he named me "Marionette." The way I see it, these are simply the consequences of my birth. Does it bother you to look like your parents, or to bear their family name?
Narzissenkreuz Institute

More than 500 years ago, four children — Alain, Mary-Ann, Jakob Baker, and Rene de Petrichor — grew up at the Narzissenkreuz Institute, a Fontaine orphanage run by the gentle Oceanid Lyris and its Vice Director, Basil Elton, former head of the White Armada. Alain and Rene became friends for many years, and as a token of friendship, Alain gave Jacob and Rene a pocket watch, which would later play an important role in their lives. At the Institute, the children loved to pretend to be Narcissus's knights, princesses, mages, and evil dragons, and Alain played the role of a knight. In the evenings, the Vice Director, Basil Elton, would tell them fairy tales, and afterward, they would eat her delicious snacks.

Five hundred years ago, when Fontaine faced the Cataclysm and Elynas, a creature from the Abyss, Basil, like many other Fontainians, went to defend the nation but never returned. Prior to her departure, the Vice Director requested that the Marechaussee Hunter and the Narzissenkreuz Institute graduate, Emanuel Guillotin, adopt Alain and Mary-Ann. Emanuel had been present at the Siege of Poisson, which left Jakob and Rene orphaned, and the experience left both physical and emotional scars. Due to this event, he left the ranks of the Marechaussee and planned to live out the rest of his days, content with just the contents of his cup, until an old friend approached him. Guillotin disliked children, but for his friend's sake, he took them in, even though he would never be a true father to them.

customize.text: Research

After graduating from the Narzissenkreuz Institute, Alain Guillotin was accepted to the Institute of Natural Philosophy, where he was recognized as a child prodigy. Many researchers at the Institute were secretly dissatisfied with his superior research resources and the dangerous mechanisms he was researching. Initially, Alain studied the Khaenri'ah mechanisms brought from Sumeru, but soon, ordinary mechanisms proved insufficient. The director managed to use government resources to acquire an odd Ruin Grader with self-repair capabilities. Rumors circulated that someone had nearly died because of these mechanisms. The mechanism once went out of control, and a researcher working with Guillotin on the project was forced to create an emergency damage control strategy in the event of a threat. The other researchers at the Institute eagerly awaited Guillotin's completion, hoping they could hold out that long. Under Alain's leadership, a "clockwork" Mek capable of releasing energy was created, leading to a breakthrough in the study of Pneumousia. His research focused on the controlled annihilation of Pneuma and Ousia. As a result, the young genius achieved a technical breakthrough and revolutionized Fontaine's energy field. Although the Institute had long observed unique forms of energy in Fontaine's atmosphere, water, and organisms, they had always been viewed as a hidden threat rather than a potential resource.

Alain Guillotin was assigned an assistant, Carter Scherbius, a former student at the Narzissenkreuz Institute. Although he considered the assistant unreliable, having caused several incidents because of him, he still visited him when he fell ill and recommended he go to Sumeru for treatment. Even when Guillotin was offered a move to a new, larger laboratory for kinematic experiments, he initially declined, worried that Carter wouldn't be able to find it. Alain was often engrossed in his research and neglected others, so Mary-Ann scolded her brother when he didn't see his adoptive father or forgot to visit Carter. After Rene de Petrichor and Jakob Ingold returned from their expedition to Sumeru, Alain recommended them to the Institute of Natural Philosophy. Later, together with his assistant and Rene, who was assigned to the same project as Alain, Guillotin studied Primordial Mechanisms and created a kinetic core based on Pneumousia. And when Alain successfully activated a controlled annihilation reaction for the first time, he, temporarily forgetting his reputation as a young genius, rushed to Rene and Jakob like any ordinary, energetic child.

Along with his younger sister, Mary-Ann, Alain became a Marechaussee Hunter, like their adoptive father. Before Alain turned twenty, he created the first prototype of a sentient Mek, Seymour, to protect Mary-Ann during her service. Alain was inspired to create Seymour by his assistant at the Institute of Natural Philosophy, Carter Scherbius, who proposed creating a sentient Kamera. He believed Alain would regret the moments he had not been with his sister, Mary-Ann, and would want to see her grow and change. Although Alain initially disapproved of the idea, he eventually saw the utility of such a development for Fontaine's Gardes.

While working at the Institute, Rene and Jakob founded a secret organization, later declared radical, the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, while Rene attempted to create Neohumans and avoid the apocalypse calculated using his world-formula. In their research, they experimented with Elynas's flesh and blood, and Jakob gained powers sustained by consuming Elynas's flesh, becoming the first Neohuman. Both Alain, the director of the Institute of Natural Philosophy, and Rene tried to help Alain's assistant, sending his samples to Sumeru, but no one found a solution to his illness. Jakob and Rene then decided to use the power of the Abyss and Eyinas's blood to save Carter, but as a result, he lost his body and his soul disintegrated. After experimenting on Carter, Alain severed all ties with Rene and Jakob. When the Marechaussee Hunters learned how far the Narzissenkreuz Ordo's research had progressed in their attempt to revive Elynas, Alain sent his Mek to the Iudex of Fontaine, Neuvillette, to warn him of the danger. Along with the Iudex, Alain Guillotin signed the decree banning the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, and the organization's headquarters remained sealed. When they signed the order to search the Tower of Gestalt, Alain looked helpless and guilty. Trying to free himself from the shackles of his body, Rene dissolved his body and severed his soul, but the experiment was unsuccessful. Only thanks to Jakob's research was he able to return. For the rest of his life, Alain regretted his inability to stop and help his best friend. As in childhood, Alain and Rene became the heroes of their own stories, with Alain continuing to play the hero, while Rene played the evil dragon. In this story, before falling into the abyss that dissolved all existence, the dragon recalled the time he once spent with the hero. And he said, <color=#ffffffd9>"Yes, hatred shall not fill me. I know that you have not seen the sights I have, and that is why you wish to stop me. The star-beasts shall drink the amniotic fluid of the world dry. A hundred years from then, all life on its surface shall be wiped away. I will surely return to save all souls. Ten years, even a hundred years may pass, but I shall be reborn as a new universe."</color> The hero, victorious over the dragon, lost what was most precious to him. He never again believed in anything that the sum of human knowledge cannot completely grasp and understand. And to the end of his days, he shall conceive of a kingdom powered by machines and energies not derived from the elements.

After the Marechaussee Phantom's battle with the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, Mary-Ann was presumed dead, leaving a lasting impression on Alain. He became even more silent and began seeing people less often. Alain opened the Mary-Ann Memorial Park in his sister's honor and left the Marechaussee Phantom, establishing the Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering. The Institute's research focused on kinetic energy and various mechanisms. During his time at the Research Institute, Alain created several Meks, some of which, like the Suppression Specialist Mek and Annihilation Specialist Mek, were named after his assistant, Carter. For his enormous contributions to research, Guillotin was named the Lord-Artificer and given the title of White Cavalier of Protection. At the ceremony where he was given the title of Lord-Artificer, all he said was the following: <color=#ffffffd9>"A quiet, humble life is a surer path to happiness than the blind pursuit of endless perfection."</color> In his old age, when Alain left the Institute, he ceased to see people. The research Guillotin conducted in his final years was never published; only traces of his work remained in his workshop.

It was named to commemorate a friend of its inventor, and was originally designed to help people. However, its ability to attack people – thereby avoiding the need to put friendly personnel at risk – subsequently came to be seen as its real strength.

customize.name: Recon Log Mek
customize.desc:
One of the earliest new-type clockwork meka to be made.

It is said that during his time at the Institute of Natural Philosophy, the Lord-Artificer Guillotin created machines that could simulate genuine intelligence.

Though he never openly admitted it, this rumor nonetheless spurred on subsequent generations of ambitious engineers. Decades ago, one of them announced that they had created a machine that not only possessed basic thinking abilities but could also read human emotions, but in the end the results went unacknowledged.

customize.name: Crimson Agate
customize.desc: A type of crystal formed from the combination of concentrated life force with an energy unique to Dragonspine. Makes for an ideal nutrient for growing Frostbearing Trees.

customize.text: Sandrone and Pulonia

After Alain Guillotin disappeared from public view, settling in a small house in the Beryl Region, he created two machines, both of which remained secret. When Alain was sixty-five, he created the intelligent machine,
in the image of the deceased Mary-Ann Guillotin. The Lord-Artificer endowed his creation with breath, taste, smell, and touch, hoping that she would have her own life to explore from every angle. Although Alain felt guilty for her creation, she was meant to be a friend and family member to alleviate his loneliness. Guillotin offered Marionette the choice of her own birthday and gave her notebooks, as journaling helped her see her soul. <color=#ffffffd9>"Much like we use wooden stakes to guide a plant to grow in a certain manner, what we choose to write down gives the soul much-needed direction. In the act of choosing what to forget and what to hold onto, we decide what kind of person we want to become."</color> At first, she threw away the notebooks after making a few notes, wondering why Alain allowed her to do so, but then she decided to keep writing in them until the end. When she told Guillotin this, Alain's composure wavered briefly, as if he wanted to cry, but didn't.

Marionette was very different in character from Mary-Ann, and Guillotin wanted her to do as she pleased. Guillotin initially created her to immortalize the years they spent with his sister together. Then he hoped that she would travel in his stead and see the world, but Marionette couldn't afford to travel because of their work. Back in his childhood, when he listened to fairy tales about evil dragons, magicians, and princesses in the orphanage, he had dreamed of saving the world, but he had long ago abandoned it. When Marionette asked if she should inherit this dream, he told her to choose her own. He once asked Marionette about her wish, but she only wanted him to be healthy. In his youth, the word "wish" seemed like such a hollow word, since you can't get everything you want, but as he got older, he began to think about dreams more often. At some point, Marionette decided she didn't like Alain at all because of his slowness and disorganization. But over time, she discovered the aspects of his character that she liked most. When she began writing in her notebook, Guillotin was surprised by these changes, and then Marionette told him that she didn't like him, but she realized her mistake and concluded that he was a very good "father." Alain was astonished for a moment, and then a smile of genuine happiness, mixed with other emotions, appeared on his face.

Alain and Marionette often read various stories, but she couldn't understand why all the fairy tales ended the same way, with the hero always winning. Alain replied that people prefer happy endings, where everything is simple and clear. Just as chess pieces are destined to follow the moves set for them, and weak people are doomed to submit to fate, so in fairy tales, the hero with a holy sword inevitably faces an evil dragon that must be defeated. So, Guillotin decided to tell a fairy tale in which the hero failed to win. Long ago, there was a kingdom ruled by a white dragon. A prophecy foretold that the kingdom was destined to perish, and even the beautiful princess would fade away with it. To save the dying world, the hero Narzissenkreuz went in search of the legendary holy sword, for only by breaking the shackles of the mundane and uniting universal aspirations could one reach the bounds of good and evil. The hero's dreams were so vast that his mortal vessel could not withstand their weight, so he longed to transcend the weakness of flesh and blood, wiping away all the world's tears, and shouldering all sin and suffering by himself. The white dragon decided to stop the hero Narzissenkreuz and built countless wicked mechanisms that defeated him. And before falling into the chasm that dissolves all existence, the hero remembered the time he once spent with the dragon and said, <color=#ffffffd9>"Yes, hatred shall not fill me. I know that you have not seen the sights I have, and that is why you wish to stop me. I will surely return to save all souls. Ten years, even a hundred years, may pass, but I shall be reborn as a new universe."</color> And for a moment, the dragon even wished for the hero to win, but the dragon wasn't so easily moved by a hero's heart, so it watched as the hero fell into the rift and vanished along with his dream. Marionette thought the hero of the tale was too arrogant, and the dragon too stubborn. They wanted to save the world, but they couldn't even understand each other's feelings, and she herself would never have done such a thing.

<color=#ffffffd9>"That's good to hear. After all, this idea of sacrificing yourself to save the world is little more than an unrealistic obsession."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"That is why stories where the righteous, kind-hearted hero wins are often more popular."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"The heroes of different stories will naturally find different holy swords, and they must also face different nemeses."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"And for all their strength and schemes, the villains will ultimately be defeated by the heroes wielding their swords..."</color>

When Alain Guillotin was nearing death, he completed his final invention, "Pulonia." Unlike Marionette, Pulonia lacked an emotional module like Sandrone, making it merely a mechanical construct. The mechanical construct was an algorithm for calculating the unknown, but even Guillotin himself didn't know what "the unknown" was. This algorithm was intended to evaluate the fate of the world and was essentially similar to the world-formula created by Rene de Petrichor. Rene's world-formula was based on the alchemical model of the "Chymical Marriage" and involved calculating constants to determine the predetermined fate of this world. When Alain first created Pulonia, Marionette believed that if a person can't control their own fate, then it's foolish to try to interfere with the fate of the world. Alain laughed, saying that there were many such fools. And although Guillotin wasn't headstrong enough, he always believed in mechanics and hoped to the end to save the world. <color=#ffffffd9>"The world can be changed. It is worth persevering."</color> However, the world's fate was too vast, and the outcome proved impossible to calculate. He waited until his death, but never received the result.

In the last days of his life, Alain was bedridden, and Marionette often felt as if he was about to break down and disappear. Guillotin dreamed of dying in a beautiful dream in which he would lie on a green lawn, gazing at the blue sky of Fontaine with his friends and sister. But Marionette was not in this dream, as she was destined to live a long life. Before his death, Alain Guillotin asked Marionette to burn all his notes when he died, so they could not be stolen. He also ordered Pulonia, whose final calculation result the Lord-Artificer had never seen, to be left to the Fontaine Research Institute. However, Marionette disliked this plan, as the staff would not be able to care for him as well as she could. After saying goodbye to Alain, Marionette read all of his research so that the great scientist's life's work would not be lost, and kept Pulonia for herself, hoping to protect the last wish and secret of her creator.

More than four hundred years later, when Sandrone had long since become the Fatui Harbinger, she was finally able to complete the Lord-Artificer's final work. By combining Rene de Petrichor's world formula with Alain's algorithm for calculating the unknown and the core from Irminsul, she created a system capable of returning the Moon Goddess, Columbina, to Teyvat from the moon's reflection. Sandrone used the Traveler as this world's "variable," as Rene had planned, and a fragment of Columbina's soul to retrieve the Moon Goddess's complete soul from the moon's reflection. The Harbinger refined the functions of Pulonia's core, converting them to work with the world formula, and implanted a new self-preservation mechanism within it so it could complete its calculations. Although Sandrone herself was forced to sacrifice her life, the algorithm for calculating the unknown successfully completed its work, returning the Moon Goddess.

After Sandrone and Pulonia's bodies were delivered to the Fontaine Research Institute, Sandrone suddenly awoke. Alain Guillotin left one final gift within her body — a second chance at life, activated by the appeared Stellar Linchpin. Because of this legacy, Sandrone was able to reboot and continue living, but the damage to Pulonia was too severe for her to repair. In addition to the second chance, Alain left Sandrone some belongings from their old home and a formula that helped her resolve her "anomaly." He believed that a person should be born twice over in their lifetime. First, there's the birth that grants people life, then the birth of the soul. The life the world gives a person and the one they choose for themselves should be separated by self-discovery, and one must consciously define the meaning of their life, instead of allowing the happenstance of their existence to pass them by. For him, Sandrone was not just a mechanism but a real person with a soul and a heart. Her computational capacity allowed her to become sentient and develop logical reasoning, but at the same time, her emotions began to conflict with her logic, creating an "anomaly." Therefore, the Lord-Artificer left Sandrone a formula that helped her to see the shape of her soul, for only by knowing what her "heart" looked like could she protect it. By understanding how the formula worked, Sandrone was able to meet her emotional self and accept it.
